BUS.G11.T2.SETUP.A1.title: Setting up a business venture
BUS.G11.T2.SETUP.A1.description: Initiating and setting up a business venture based on an action plan to generate income, and acquiring funding where needed — equity capital, loans/debt capital and other sources of capital.
BUS.G11.T2.SETUP.A1.strand: T2 — Creative thinking, stress & change, action plans, setting up, ethics & presentation
BUS.G11.T2.SETUP.A1.recovery_strategy: Equity capital = the owner's own money or money from investors (no repayment, but shared ownership). Loan/debt capital = borrowed money that must be repaid with interest. A new venture is set up by working through its action plan and securing funding.

questions.question: Money the owner or investors put into a business, which need not be repaid like a loan, is called _________ capital.
questions.memo: Equity capital is the owners' or investors' own money. It is not repaid like a loan, but it gives investors a share of ownership.

questions.question: A bank loan is an example of _________ capital.
questions.memo: Borrowed money such as a bank loan is loan or debt capital, which must be repaid with interest.

questions.question: True or false: Loan capital must be repaid, usually with interest.
questions.memo: Loan (debt) capital is borrowed, so it must be paid back over time, normally with interest added.

questions.question: Setting up a new venture should be based on the business's _________ plan.
questions.memo: A venture is set up by working through the action plan — the list of dated, assigned tasks that turn the idea into a real business.

questions.question: True or false: Equity capital does not have to be repaid in the way a loan does.
questions.memo: Equity is not a loan, so there are no fixed repayments — but investors expect a share of ownership and profit in return.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of setting up a business venture?
options: To keep the idea secret forever
questions.memo: A venture is set up to trade and generate income for its owners.

questions.question: Sort each source of funding into equity capital or loan/debt capital.

items.text: Money from investors in exchange for shares
Profit kept in the business (retained profit)
Credit from a supplier that must be repaid

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Owners' savings, investor share money and retained profit are equity. Bank loans, overdrafts and supplier credit are debt that must be repaid.

questions.question: What is an advantage of equity capital over loan capital?
options: There are no fixed repayments or interest
It always comes from a bank
It must be repaid within a month
questions.expected: There are no fixed repayments or interest
questions.memo: Equity has no compulsory repayments or interest, which eases pressure on a new business's cash flow.

questions.question: What is a disadvantage of raising equity capital from investors?
options: The owner has to share ownership and profit
The money must be repaid with high interest
It can never be used to grow the business
questions.expected: The owner has to share ownership and profit
questions.memo: Investors who provide equity take a share of the business and its profits, so the original owner gives up some control and reward.

questions.question: A _________ is borrowed money that a business must repay over time.
questions.memo: A loan is borrowed money that must be repaid, usually in instalments with interest.

questions.question: True or false: The business plan and action plan guide how a venture is set up.
questions.memo: The business plan sets out the idea and the action plan turns it into tasks, together guiding the setting up of the venture.

questions.question: Thesis: 'A new venture should fund itself with a mix of the owner's own equity and not only loans.' Choose the THREE strongest supporting reasons.
questions.thesis: A new venture should fund itself with a mix of the owner's own equity and not only loans.

pool.text: Equity has no fixed repayments, easing cash-flow pressure early on
Investing own money shows commitment and reassures lenders
Too much debt means heavy repayments that can sink a young business
Equity must always be repaid faster than any loan
The owner likes the look of the bank's logo
Loans are never useful for any business

questions.memo: The strong reasons are easier cash flow, showing commitment, and avoiding crippling debt. The others are false or irrelevant.

questions.question: Why might a founder prefer a loan rather than bringing in equity investors?
options: A loan lets the founder keep full ownership of the business
A loan never has to be repaid
A loan gives investors control of the business
A loan charges no interest at all
questions.expected: A loan lets the founder keep full ownership of the business
questions.memo: With a loan the founder keeps full ownership; equity investors would take a share of the business in return for their money.

questions.question: Sort each statement under the funding choice it best supports.

items.text: You want to avoid fixed monthly repayments
You are willing to share profit with investors
You can comfortably afford regular repayments
Cash flow is uncertain in the early months
You do not want to give away any control

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Equity suits those who want no repayments and will share ownership; a loan suits those who can afford repayments and want to keep full control.

questions.question: What is a sensible first step when actually setting up a venture from an action plan?
options: Work through the action-plan tasks and secure the funding needed
Spend all the money before any plan is made
questions.expected: Work through the action-plan tasks and secure the funding needed
questions.memo: Setting up means following the action plan and arranging the capital required so the tasks can be carried out.

questions.question: Interest is best described as the _________ of borrowing money.
questions.memo: Interest is the cost a borrower pays a lender for the use of money over time.

questions.question: An early-stage venture has very uncertain income. Which funding choice usually puts less pressure on it, and why?
options: Equity, because there are no fixed repayments while income is uncertain
A large loan, because the repayments are comforting
A loan, because interest reduces risk
Neither, because funding is never needed
questions.expected: Equity, because there are no fixed repayments while income is uncertain
questions.memo: When income is unpredictable, equity is safer because the business is not forced to make fixed loan repayments it may not be able to afford.

questions.question: Why can relying too heavily on loans be risky for a brand-new business?
options: High repayments and interest can sink the business before it becomes profitable
Loans make a business impossible to register
Loans remove the owner's need to work
questions.expected: High repayments and interest can sink the business before it becomes profitable
questions.memo: Heavy debt means large fixed repayments that a young, not-yet-profitable business may struggle to meet, threatening its survival.

questions.question: Why do many ventures use a mix of equity and loan capital rather than only one?
options: It balances keeping control with limiting repayment pressure
It is required by law to use both
It doubles the amount that must be repaid for no reason
It guarantees the business cannot fail
questions.expected: It balances keeping control with limiting repayment pressure
questions.memo: A blend lets the owner keep some control (loans) while easing cash-flow pressure (equity), spreading the risks of each.

questions.question: A founder launches following the action plan but has not arranged any funding. What is the likely result?
options: The venture stalls, because tasks cannot be paid for without capital
The venture runs perfectly without any money
Funding appears automatically once trading starts
Capital is never needed to set up a business
questions.expected: The venture stalls, because tasks cannot be paid for without capital
questions.memo: Even a good action plan needs capital to fund its tasks; without securing funding, the setup quickly stalls.
